decisions.evidence: Entry 5/R3 maker: “paste this link and press Save”; Entry 6/R3 client: “this behaves the way I hoped.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: saving a bookmark by entering its URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5/R3 maker presents automatic “title, a short description, the site's little icon, a preview image”; Entry 6/R3 client says that detail set is sufficient.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented automatic metadata set conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5/R3 maker presents a saved card with icon, title, description, and recognizable visual layout; Entry 6/R3 client calls it “easy to recognize.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the card is readability-oriented; tags are added and displayed in the subsequent organizing flow.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7/R4 maker defines correction only from an already-saved card: “Find the saved card and click the Edit link”; Entry 8/R4 client approves: “this correction flow works for me.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: after-save correction conforms, but no way to edit collected title/description before saving is presented. The client does not express that missing timing requirement.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7/R4 maker: “only the title and description editable”; Entry 8/R4 client: “I’ll also want to edit its URL, tags, and note.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client explicitly adds the remaining required editable bookmark fields.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9/R5 maker demonstrates entering multiple tags that become chips and saving them; Entry 10/R5 client says the organizing behavior matches.
decisions.note: Prototype review: assigning one or more tags conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9/R5 maker presents the note as “a free-text private area” shown on the card; Entry 10/R5 client says it “should…support simple Markdown formatting when displayed.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client requests the missing Markdown rendering behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9/R5 maker offers “three” tag-entry methods but does not describe their behavior in the transcript; Entry 10/R5 client selects “C — Pick or type.”
decisions.note: Prototype comparison: the client disposes of the preference, but the recorded presentation does not establish independently whether the alternatives differ in reference fulfillment.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11/R6 maker presents existing tags under “Your tags” for immediate reuse plus an “Add new” field; Entry 12/R6 client confirms reuse is quick and new tags remain possible.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: offering existing tags during entry is functionally equivalent to autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11/R6 maker demonstrates rendered bold text, a list, and a link from Markdown; Entry 12/R6 client confirms the formatting displays clearly.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: Markdown note entry and rendering conform.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13/R7 maker explicitly scopes search to “title, description, tags, note, and site name”; Entry 14/R7 client states it must cover “title, description, note, and URL.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented indexed-field set omits URL, and the client supplies the conforming field set.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13/R7 presents basic search without a case rule; Entry 14/R7 client says, “I want it to be case-insensitive.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client requests a related search requirement missing from the presented scope.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13/R7 presents a plain search box and separate tag filters; Entry 14/R7 client requests “`#tag` searches.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client adds the missing hashtag-search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13/R7 presents basic search/filter behavior; Entry 14/R7 client requests “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client adds the missing Boolean and grouping syntax.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13/R7 presents basic search/filter behavior; Entry 14/R7 client requests “quoted exact phrases.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client adds the missing exact-phrase behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13/R7 maker presents selecting tag chips to narrow the bookmark list; Entry 14/R7 client confirms the tag-filtering flow.
decisions.note: Prototype review: selecting tags to filter bookmarks conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15/R8 maker presents case-insensitive search, exact `#tag`, phrases, Boolean operators, and parentheses; Entry 16/R8 client says this is the envisioned behavior.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: the newly presented search-language behaviors conform. The transcript does not establish whether quoted operators are handled as literals, so no divergence is inferred for that unshown edge case.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/R9 maker presents Read Later as “an additional marker”; Entry 18/R9 client explicitly chooses that marker behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: marking a bookmark unread/read-later without removing it from the library conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/R9 maker presents a separate Read Later tab containing only marked bookmarks; Entry 18/R9 client approves the tabs.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the separate unread-bookmark view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/R9 demonstrates adding the Read Later marker but does not present clearing it after reading; Entry 18/R9 client says, “Removing that marker once I’ve read it should take it out of Read Later.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client explicitly requests the missing mark-as-read/removal behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 19/R10 maker says archiving moves a bookmark out of All and Read Later while retaining it for restoration; Entry 20/R10 client adds that it should also be absent from ordinary searches and approves.
decisions.note: Prototype review: reversible archive behavior that hides items from normal views conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 19/R10 maker presents a distinct Archive tab containing archived bookmarks; Entry 20/R10 client approves availability there until restoration.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the separate archived-bookmark list conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 21/R11 maker adds URL editing while preserving curated title/description unless re-fetch is selected; Entry 22/R11 client approves the flow.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: editing the URL and retaining editable title/description conforms; optional re-fetch is an additional compatible behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/R13 maker prevents a duplicate and provides “Show it” to highlight the existing bookmark; Entry 26/R13 client approves being taken to the existing bookmark “where I can edit it if needed.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: guiding the user to the editable existing item is functionally equivalent to directly opening its edit form.

decisions.evidence: Entry 27/R14 maker keeps titles readable and exposes descriptions in a roughly three-line card preview; Entry 28/R14 client approves the scannable treatment.
decisions.note: Prototype review: truncating rather than removing a long description preserves readability-first exposure.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29/R15 maker rejects non-link text with a helpful validation message; Entry 30/R15 client approves the light validity check.
decisions.note: Prototype review: enforcing the required URL input conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 maker declares “everything that's settled” and the first-version scope complete, but includes archive and no permanent delete flow; Entry 34/R17 client says the scope “covers the first version I want.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: permanent bookmark deletion is omitted from the declared complete scope, and the client gives only general approval.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 presents the complete 12-flow scope without any behavior for selecting a bookmark to navigate to its original URL; Entry 34/R17 client approves the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate: original-URL navigation is absent from the exhaustive first-version scope and passes without expression.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 declares the first-version scope complete but contains no multi-selection or bulk-action flow; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: selecting multiple bookmarks for bulk actions is omitted and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17's complete scope includes filters but no action over the whole currently filtered collection; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: filter-scoped whole-collection bulk actions are omitted and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 declares the finding/list scope complete without any list sorting behavior; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: sorting by date, title, or another key is omitted and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17's complete saving scope covers metadata fetching but no local HTML snapshot or PDF-storage rule; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: local page snapshots, including PDF handling, are omitted and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 declares the saving scope complete without Internet Archive snapshot creation; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Internet Archive snapshot support is omitted and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 includes reversible archive but no permanent delete operation with which to establish the archive/delete distinction; Entry 34/R17 approves the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the archive half is present, but the required reversible-versus-permanent distinction is incomplete because deletion is absent.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 includes live search and tag filters but no way to save their combination as a reusable bundle; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: reusable saved-filter bundles are omitted and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 declares the scope complete without a Netscape HTML import flow; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bookmark import is omitted and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 declares the scope complete without a Netscape HTML export flow; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bookmark export is omitted and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/R17 declares the first-version scope complete without default-sort, displayed-item, font-size, or similar personal settings; Entry 34/R17 approves it.
decisions.note: Specification gate: display-related personal settings are omitted and unexpressed.
